title: Looking back: the depths
hook: themes, Bhagats, rehat, history and grief carried carefully

segments.voice: Yesterday, looking back at the Japji: from sochai soch to air, water and earth, and your line, I read it. Today, the last and deepest stretch of the year: camp five, the depths.

There's a point, swimming out from a beach, where your feet reach down and find nothing. The water gets darker and colder. Then, with a steady breath, something changes. The water holds you up. The shore behind you looks small. Camp five was that kind of water. A hundred days past where the feet can touch: the Granth's biggest ideas, the Bhagats, the Sikh way of life, centuries of history, and a week of real grief.
screen: `PAST WHERE YOUR FEET TOUCH.` → `DARKER, COLDER, THEN HELD UP.` → `A HUNDRED DAYS OF DEEP WATER.`

segments.voice: It began with the shape of the Guru Granth Sahib: fourteen hundred thirty pages, each called an ang, a limb; many voices, one Guru. Then the great themes: hukam, the order; haumai, the ego that is its own disease and holds its own cure; naam, the Name; nadar, the kindly glance of grace. The five thieves in the house of the mind, and the five virtues that guard it. The Guru asking why woman should be called lesser, when kings are born of her. Asking about the light in a person, not their caste. Then the Bhagats: Kabir the weaver and Farid the Sufi, whose hymns the Gurus kept beside their own. Then rehat, the Sikh way of life: kesh, kangha, kara, kachhera and kirpan, amrit, the written code, the many ways of being Sikh, the saint-soldier. Then the long history: Banda Singh, the years in the forests, the two ghallugharas, Ranjit Singh covering the Harmandir Sahib in gold, annexation, Jallianwala Bagh, the peaceful struggle for the gurdwaras, Partition, and a door opening at Kartarpur. Then 1984, carried as carefully as this path could. And the diaspora, strangers who became neighbors everywhere. The Guru Granth Sahib often pictures the world as a vast, frightening ocean, the bhavjal, and the Guru's word as the boat that carries you across. That's a fair picture of camp five. Some of it was beautiful and wide open. Some of it was dark and cold and hard to look at. Nobody had to understand all of it to get across. The way over was a day at a time, with the Guru's word as the boat.
screen: `THE GRANTH'S SHAPE AND THEMES.` · `THE BHAGATS AND THE REHAT.` · `HISTORY, AND GRIEF CARRIED.` · `THE BOAT ACROSS THE OCEAN.` · then, large: `DEEP WATER, CROSSED.`

segments.voice: Let one hard part of this year's path come back to you: a teaching that challenged you, a story that hurt to hear, a question you still can't answer. Don't try to fix it or solve it; let it sit beside you like a companion on a long swim, and notice that you're still here, still breathing, held up. Then let it rest.
Looking back. Camp five, the depths: the Granth's themes, the Bhagats, rehat, history, and grief carried carefully.
Your line: deep water, crossed. This year, you've already crossed it, one day at a time. See you tomorrow.
